findings.title: Cached IDP list is not safe when organization membership changes or an org is invalidated
findings.body: The login cache key contains only realm and fetch mode, so each search (per organizationId) is stored in a single IdentityProviderListQuery. Invalidation happens only when an IDP's login status or organization link changes. getByOrganization also checks isInvalid(orgId), but getForLogin does not. Org-level changes such as deleting an org or removing its IDPs can therefore leave stale results. The wrapped enabled state is also not part of the cached ids. Deleting an org or unlinking an IDP through the organization API may not hit the registerIDPLoginInvalidation path, depending on whether it goes through update().

findings.title: remove() may NPE or change behavior for a missing alias
findings.body: storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is now fetched unconditionally. If the alias does not exist it is null. When isInvalid(cacheKey) is true, registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) dereferences it and throws a NullPointerException. This path previously only ran in the invalid case. registerIDPLoginInvalidation tolerates null via the predicate's nonNull check, but the first call does not. remove() on a nonexistent alias should return false. The extra DB query on every removal is also unnecessary when the cache already holds the IDP.

findings.title: Set-based result loses ordering and may return disabled IDPs
findings.body: Results are collected into a HashSet and the cached ids are a Set, so any ordering from the delegate is lost. getById returns org-aware wrappers whose isEnabled depends on the organization's state. Callers that don't re-check isEnabled would get disabled IDPs, because the cache holds IDs computed with the original enabled state. Only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean was patched, and not the REALM_ONLY path.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed for non-cache users
findings.body: The added clause makes an org-linked IDP count as a login IDP only if BROKER_PUBLIC is true. This changes a shared SPI predicate. It also calls idp.getConfig().get(...), which NPEs if the config is null. The change is only justified for cache invalidation, but it alters public behaviour for any other user of the predicate.

findings.title: Cleanup registered for the wrong alias
findings.body: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal "alias" instead of the created alias. The created IDPs are never cleaned up and may leak into other tests. The same bug exists at line 303 and is copied here.
